title: FRONTIER Act
committees: House Energy and Commerce; House Science, Space, and Technology
summary: Creates a federal framework for covered frontier-model developers using compute and developer-size thresholds. It combines risk-management duties, third-party audits, mandatory incident reporting, emergency authority, and targeted state-law preemption with savings clauses.
committee_dynamics: The dual referral is a major jurisdictional constraint. House Science has moved narrower bipartisan AI-security bills, while Energy and Commerce controls important commercial and enforcement questions. Preemption is likely to be the hardest bargaining issue.
advance_rationale: Bipartisan architecture and committee-chair sponsorship make the bill consequential, but its late introduction, dual referral, enforcement design, and preemption language raise substantial transaction costs.

title: Secure AI Development Act
summary: Establishes secure pre-release testing for frontier AI, modernizes vulnerability reporting, reviews AI vulnerabilities under the federal Vulnerabilities Equities Process, and strengthens NSA AI Security Center and laboratory/system-security functions.
committee_dynamics: Warner brings intelligence and cyber credibility, but Senate Commerce has jurisdiction over the civilian standards and development provisions. The bill may move more readily as intelligence-authorization or NDAA text than as a standalone measure.
advance_rationale: Strong national-security framing and natural must-pass vehicles offset the absence of public markup and the need to coordinate Commerce and intelligence equities.

advance_rationale: Limited coalition and no committee action make standalone passage difficult, although the reporting concepts are plausible amendment material.
